items.title: Al Rose Interview, 1976-02-24
items.q: I have worked with Charlie Parker and I have recorded Charlie Parker

ctx.x: Now, it's been said that, and I think Frank Power said this in a tape that he did in Bidebeck's life, that there was only one other musician that bare any resemblance to Bix Bidebeck. In the sense that both these musicians were victimized by the changing values of their time. And he mentions Charlie Parker. Now, I don't want to talk about, I don't want to bring up Charlie Parker. I'd rather talk about Bix Bidebeck. But, it's very interesting to me that he should bring up Charlie Parker in the relationship to Bix…

Well, it may have dramatized it to some extent, but I believe that the decline of the actualities behind the dream had already begun sometime earlier than that. I believe firmly that the American system has been in decline, demonstrably in decline, since the beginning of World War I. As far as the application of Charlie Parker, of course, I knew Charlie Parker and I didn't know Big Spider-Bank. However, it's fair to say that I know more about Big Spider-Bank than I know about Charlie Parker. In the first place,…
You don't understand the basis of his appeal?

items.title: Al Rose Interview, 1976-02-19
items.q: I know that you've had dealings with him in your own recording industry to a certain extent at work... I considered that Charlie Parker was very pleasant. He had a tendency to be narcissistic. He was friendly but unresponsive to people around him.

ctx.x: and that's Charlie Parker. I know that you've had dealings with him in your own recording industry to a certain extent at work. But would you say that Charlie Parker's a great musician?

No. I would say that Charlie Parker was a musician who developed high skills in doing particular things that were of interest to him. But I wouldn't say that he was a great musician, certainly not that. I would say that his music is, of course, largely influenced by Rudy Valli, according to...
This is something I don't quite understand.
